title: If, Else If, Else
summary: Choose between branches with else and else if, and order the conditions so the right branch wins.
intro: An `if` alone can only skip code. Add `else` and `else if` and your program picks exactly one path out of several.

steps.title: else

example.title: Odd or even, pass or fail
example.prompt: Print whether 7 is odd or even, then print Pass or Fail for a score of 72 with a pass mark of 60.
example.explanation: `7%2` is 1, so `n%2 == 0` is false and the `else` block prints `7 is odd`. For the score, `72 >= 60` is true, so the `if` block prints `Pass` and the `else` block is skipped.

practice.title: Debt and stock
practice.prompt:
Print an account status and a stock status, each chosen with an if and an else.

1. With `balance := -15`, print `In debt` when the balance is below 0, otherwise `In credit`.
2. With `stock := 0`, print `Sold out` when the stock is 0, otherwise `Available`.
3. Remove the `_ =` lines and the placeholder `fmt.Println()` once you use the variables.

Expected output:

```text
In debt
Sold out
```
hints: Each status needs one `if` and one `else`: the `if` block prints the first word and the `else` block prints the other.
The conditions are `balance < 0` and `stock == 0`. Keep each `} else {` on the line of the closing brace.

steps.title: else if chains

example.title: Letter grade
example.prompt: Turn a score of 83 into a letter grade: 90 and up is A, 80 and up is B, 70 and up is C, anything lower is F.
example.explanation: `83 >= 90` is false, so Go moves on. `83 >= 80` is true, so `grade` becomes `"B"` and the rest of the chain is skipped, including `83 >= 70`, which is also true. `grade` was declared before the chain, so it still exists for the final `fmt.Println`.

practice.title: Shipping tier
practice.prompt:
Turn a parcel weight into a shipping tier with an if, else if, else chain.

1. Use `weight := 3.2` (kilograms).
2. Set `tier` to `Small` under 1, `Medium` under 5, `Large` under 20, and `Freight` otherwise.
3. Print `Tier:` followed by a space and the tier.

Expected output:

```text
Tier: Medium
```
hints: These checks use `<`, so start with the smallest limit: `if weight < 1 {`.
Assign with `tier = "Medium"`, not `:=`, so the outer `tier` changes.

steps.title: Nested conditions

example.title: Leap years
example.prompt: Decide whether 1900 is a leap year with nested ifs, then decide for 2024 with a single condition.
example.output:
1900 is not a leap year
2024 is a leap year
example.explanation: 1900 is divisible by 4, so Go enters the outer block. It is also divisible by 100, so it enters the next one. It is not divisible by 400, so the innermost `else` runs. For 2024, `year%4 == 0` is true and `year%100 != 0` is true, so `||` short-circuits and the whole condition is true.

practice.title: Free shipping
practice.prompt:
Shipping is free from 25 dollars for members and from 50 dollars for everyone else. Decide two orders, first with nested ifs and then with one condition.

1. With `member := true` and `order := 30`, write `if member { ... } else { ... }` with an if/else on `order` inside each branch (25 for members, 50 otherwise).
2. Then with `member = false` and `order = 40`, decide with one if/else on `order >= 50 || (member && order >= 25)`.
3. Print each result with `fmt.Printf` as `Order <amount>: free shipping` or `Order <amount>: pay shipping`.
4. Remove the `_ =` lines and the placeholder `fmt.Println()`.

Expected output:

```text
Order 30: free shipping
Order 40: pay shipping
```

tests.output:
Order 30: free shipping
Order 40: pay shipping

hints: Inside `if member {` write `if order >= 25 {` with an `else`. Inside the outer `else`, do the same with 50.
In the `fmt.Printf` format, `%d` stands for the amount and `\n` ends the line. `fmt.Println("Order", order, ":")` would put a space before the colon.

recap:
- `if cond { } else { }` runs exactly one of the two blocks.
- Keep `} else {` on one line, or automatic semicolon insertion breaks the code.
- In an `else if` chain only the first true branch runs, so put the most specific condition first.
- Declare a result with `var` before the chain and assign it with `=` in each branch.
- Nest an `if` inside an `if` or `else` when rules refine each other.
- Nested ifs with no `else` fold into `&&`, alternative paths fold into `||`, and parentheses keep the grouping clear.
